name: response-statistics-v1
hypothesis: User-disjoint, smoothed response statistics for product and anonymous ad attributes, including interactions with context cat0/cat1, transfer candidate-level response information to other users and unseen products.
training: Same three outer/inner user assignments and fit-only base transformers as candidate-count reproduction. Reuse nine frozen full BCE/LogLoss baseline models. Train two feature variants x3 folds x3 seeds=18 new BCE models with identical baseline hyperparameters and LogLoss early stopping. No parameter tuning. ad_stats adds24 numeric statistics to48 features; ad_context_stats adds76 to48. Product IDs are lookup keys, not raw model inputs. Keep all fit rows. Freeze all18 checkpoints and all full-fit statistics before producing any new outer predictions.
leakage_contract: Within each outer fit partition, assign USERS by SHA256 to five encoding folds. Each fit row receives statistics from the OTHER four user folds, including the global prior and all hierarchical priors; exclude every row of its user, not just the current row. Inner and held statistics are fitted only on outer FIT users, never inner or held labels. Transform only receives label-free keys. No user label history, original rank, displayrandom or protected columns enter the features. Cross-fitting is user-disjoint, not sklearn default row-wise TargetEncoder. No time field exists, so this does not establish point-in-time validity.
features: All stats come from observed sampled rows. Global p=(clicks+0.5)/(rows+1). cat2..cat12 and context cat0/cat1 rates shrink toward global p with strength100. Product rate shrinks toward the mean of its11 attribute rates with strength20. Attribute x context rate shrinks with100 toward sigmoid(logit(attribute p)+logit(context p)-logit(global p)). Product x context rate shrinks with20 toward mean11 attribute x context rates. Each table produces smoothed rate and log1p source row count. Unseen keys have count0 and exactly their parent prior. No semantic meanings are assigned to anonymous categories. Fixed smoothing constants, no outer tuning.
primary_test: ad_context_stats minus existing BCE/LogLoss tie-expected Top1 observed click capture on randomized-display multi-candidate requests, all zero-click requests included. Support requires positive point differences in each of3 user folds, pooled paired whole-user bootstrap95% lower bound>0, and pooled all-display lower bound>0. Primary arm cannot be switched after results.
cold_start: Fit-unseen means product absent from fit. STRICT unseen means absent from BOTH fit and inner feature IDs; stricter than unavailable response stats. Status uses IDs only. Report strict-all-cold requests separately. For mixed/full candidate requests containing a strict-unseen product, keep the entire candidate list and compute captured clicks credited ONLY to strict-unseen ads, plus selected-cold exposure and total utility. No credit for selecting a known clicked ad in the cold metric. Cold support is a secondary exploratory claim requiring positive cold-capture points in all3 folds, pooled all-display and randomized has-cold95% lower bounds>0. Also report fit-unseen and strict-unseen row LogLoss/AUC, but they do not establish ranking benefit. All-cold counts were inspected without labels before protocol:533 multi requests pooled.
secondary: ad_stats vs baseline; context interactions vs marginal stats; full-list Top3; seen/mixed/all-cold cohorts; first-time-product response probability metrics. All auxiliary intervals descriptive and unadjusted for multiple testing. No cohort threshold search or fallback tuning after outcomes.
aggregation: Average per-request outcomes over3 seed fits, not scores/ensembles. Every original-train user evaluated once. Paired bootstrap resamples whole users and conditions on frozen models; training sets overlap across folds. Known development pool, not independent test data.
limitations: Original validation/test are not read. Counts and rates reflect sampled historical logs, not population CTR or exposure propensity. No temporal ordering available: statistics are cross-user development features, not audited past-only serving history. Observed click capture is not online incremental CTR/revenue. Existing service/champion stays unchanged.
